contradictions.fact: Approach distance from Pete Lake Trailhead to Vista Lakes camp

claims.says: making this a two-day approach of about 9 miles and 2,800 ft to reach the alpine basin

contradictions.why: The route's own approach prose and approach_variants[0] put the one-way distance to Vista Lakes camp at 9-10 miles, but the itinerary day-1 mileage and the Vista Lakes waypoint both give 13 miles for the same leg -- a 30-40% swing.
contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft for the leg (2,800 ft) is identical in both the approach prose and itinerary.days[0], confirming they describe the same segment; the itinerary/waypoint figure (13 mi) is corroborated by descent_text's independently-stated round-trip total ('approximately 30-33+ miles' ≈ 13 mi one-way x2 + summit push), so the approach prose's '9 miles' and approach_variants' distMi 10 are the likely outliers.

contradictions.fact: Total elevation gain/loss for the route

claims.says: about 10 miles round trip and 3,500 ft of gain

contradictions.why: gain_ft/loss_ft claim 6,300 ft, but the itinerary's own day total and totalNote claim only 3,500 ft — and 3,500 ft is impossible on its own terms, since the trailhead (2,400 ft) to the summit (6,693 ft) is already a 4,333 ft net elevation gain, more than the itinerary's claimed cumulative total.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary's 3,500 ft is mathematically inconsistent with the route's own trailhead/summit elevations (net gain 4,333 ft exceeds the claimed cumulative gain of 3,500 ft); gain_ft/loss_ft (6,300 ft) is the plausible figure. (Also flagged by the mechanical detector.)
